title: A Comprehensive Guide to the SASSA Means Test
description: The SASSA means test is a crucial part of the grant application process. This guide will help you understand what it is, how it works, and whether you qualify.

steps.title: What is the Means Test?
steps.content: The means test is an assessment used by SASSA to determine if your income and assets are below a certain limit. This limit is called the 'threshold'. If your means are above the threshold, you will not qualify for a grant. The means test ensures that only those who are truly in need receive financial assistance from the government.
tips: The means test is different for each type of grant.
Your spouse's income and assets may also be considered.

steps.title: Income Thresholds
steps.content:
The income threshold is the maximum amount of money you can earn per month and still qualify for a grant. As of 2026, the income thresholds for the most common grants are:
  • Old Age Grant: R7,920 per month for a single person, or R15,840 combined for a married couple.
  • Disability Grant: R7,920 per month for a single person, or R15,840 combined for a married couple.
  • Child Support Grant: R5,280 per month for a single caregiver, or R10,560 combined for a married couple.
tips: Income includes salaries, wages, pensions, and any other regular payments you receive.
The SRD grant has a much lower income threshold of R624 per month.

steps.title: Asset Thresholds
steps.content:
The asset threshold is the maximum value of assets you can own and still qualify for a grant. Assets include things like property, vehicles, and investments. As of 2026, the asset thresholds are:
  • Old Age Grant: R1,227,600 for a single person, or R2,455,200 for a married couple.
  • Disability Grant: R1,227,600 for a single person, or R2,455,200 for a married couple.
tips: The value of the home you live in is not included in the asset test.
Child Support Grant does not have an asset test.

title: How to Reinstate a Lapsed or Suspended Grant
description: If your SASSA grant has been suspended or has lapsed, don't panic. This guide will walk you through the steps to get it reinstated.

steps.title: Why was my grant suspended?
steps.content:
A grant can be suspended for several reasons, including:
  • A change in your financial circumstances.
  • Failure to collect the grant for three consecutive months.
  • You were admitted to a state institution for more than three months.
  • You are no longer eligible for the grant.
tips: SASSA should send you a letter explaining why your grant was suspended.
You can also check your status online or by calling the SASSA helpline.

steps.title: How to apply for restoration
steps.content:
To have your grant reinstated, you must apply for restoration within 90 days of the suspension. You will need to visit your nearest SASSA office and bring the following documents:
  • Your 13-digit bar-coded ID.
  • Proof of your current address.
  • Any documents that prove you are still eligible for the grant (e.g., a recent payslip, a doctor's letter).
tips: There is no fee to apply for restoration.
If you are too sick to visit a SASSA office, you can have someone apply on your behalf.

steps.title: What happens next?
steps.content: SASSA will review your application for restoration. If your application is successful, your grant will be reinstated and you will receive back payments from the date it was suspended. If your application is denied, you have the right to appeal the decision.
tips: The restoration process can take up to three months.
Keep your receipt as proof of your application.

title: Understanding and Reporting SASSA Fraud
description: SASSA fraud is a serious crime that affects everyone. This guide will help you understand what it is and how you can help to stop it.

steps.title: What is SASSA fraud?
steps.content:
SASSA fraud is any act that is intended to deceive SASSA into paying a grant to someone who is not entitled to it. This includes:
  • Applying for a grant with false information.
  • Not telling SASSA about changes in your circumstances.
  • Someone else using your SASSA card without your permission.
  • Moneylenders taking your SASSA card as security for a loan.
tips: If you are not sure if something is fraud, it is better to report it.

steps.title: How to report fraud
steps.content:
If you suspect that someone is committing SASSA fraud, you should report it immediately. You can report fraud in any of the following ways:
  • Call the SASSA toll-free fraud hotline on 0800 60 10 11.
  • Report it to your nearest police station.
  • Report it to your nearest SASSA office.
tips: Provide as much information as possible when you report fraud.
You do not have to give your name when you report fraud.
